🕯️ Remembering Chuck Norris

March 10, 1940 — March 19, 2026 · A life fully lived

The Boy from Oklahoma

Born Carlos Ray Norris on March 10, 1940, in Ryan, Oklahoma, Chuck grew up in a modest family and was described as a shy, quiet child. His father served in WWII and young Chuck found discipline through the United States Air Force — where he first encountered martial arts in South Korea and never looked back.

That shy Oklahoma boy would go on to become a six-time undefeated World Karate Champion, a Hollywood action legend, and the greatest internet meme of all time.

A Heart Full of Love

Chuck married Gena O'Kelley in November 1998. Together they had twins Dakota and Danilee, born in 2001. He was a devoted father to five children and grandfather to 13 grandchildren.

For their 23rd anniversary he wrote: "My love, my life, my best friend, my world. I love you with all my heart." Gena was by his side when he passed peacefully in Hawaii on March 19, 2026.

Warrior. Patriot. Icon.

Chuck Norris was made an Honorary U.S. Marine, jogged with two U.S. Presidents, visited troops in Iraq and Afghanistan, and dedicated his life to supporting veterans and military families through his charities.

His family's final statement: "To the world, he was a martial artist, actor, and a symbol of strength. To us, he was a devoted husband, a loving father and grandfather, an incredible brother, and the heart of our family."

His Final Words to the World

On March 10, 2026 — just 9 days before he passed — Chuck celebrated his 86th birthday by posting a video of himself boxing. Fists up, eyes sharp, still fighting.

His caption: "I don't age… I level up." 🥊

That was Chuck Norris. Never stopping. Never surrendering. Even at 86. The legend never dies.
